summary: Frontend-only validation of MOOD for DESIGN™ Sidebar Architecture v4. Logged in as demo@moodfordesign.com (super-admin), verified the complete sidebar structure, ™ discipline, collapse persistence, active states, ComingSoonPage rendering, redirects and canonical routes. Overall result: PASS — all 17 spec items verified. One minor visual discrepancy: the active-state left accent strip computes to rgb(0,201,179) (teal) instead of gold #d9b285 because the CSS variable --bp-primary is set to teal at the theme level (the code uses `var(--bp-primary,#d9b285)` so the fallback gold is shadowed). The background tint IS correctly gold rgba(217,178,133,0.05). No SaaS blue is present.

ui_bugs.issue: Active left-accent vertical strip renders TEAL rgb(0,201,179) instead of architectural gold #d9b285. Cause: CSS var --bp-primary is bound to teal at the theme root, so `bg-[var(--bp-primary,#d9b285)]` resolves to teal. The 5% background tint is correctly gold (rgba(217,178,133,0.05)). Spec mandated gold accent — currently the accent visually conflicts with the gold tint.

issues: Accent strip color (teal) inconsistent with gold tint — visual dissonance; consider hard-coding #d9b285 or aliasing a dedicated --bp-accent-gold variable.

action_items: Decide gold-vs-teal for the active-state left accent. Either (a) hard-code `bg-[#d9b285]` on the accent span in Sidebar.jsx NavItem (line ~78), or (b) introduce a dedicated CSS var --bp-accent-gold so the theme-level --bp-primary (teal) does not shadow the gold fallback. Per spec the accent MUST be gold #d9b285.
critical_code_review_comments: Sidebar.jsx line 78: `bg-[var(--bp-primary,#d9b285)]` — the CSS fallback only fires when --bp-primary is undefined. In the current theme --bp-primary resolves to teal #00c9b3, so the gold-fallback is dead code. Use an explicit gold token to enforce the architectural color.
ComingSoonPage.jsx: clean editorial implementation; Italian copy and slug-driven content are correct. Consider adding `aria-current` semantics for the active sidebar entry to improve accessibility.

Sidebar.jsx Section component: when sidebar is collapsed (icon-mode) the section toggle button is not rendered (Section returns just a separator) — this is fine for UX but means automated tests must expand the sidebar before exercising toggle persistence. Documented for next testers.

When sidebar is in icon-mode, section toggle buttons are hidden — expand first. Demo super-admin has both isSuperAdmin and tenant:settings capability so admin-gated items (Project Studio, full Content Studio section, Brand Studio/Forms & Journeys/Integrations/Billing/Settings in Studio OS, and Platform section) are visible. ™ symbol present in DOM exactly twice in sidebar: 'Design Journey™' and 'Cultural Editions™'. The only outstanding spec mismatch is the active accent color (teal vs gold) — see action_items.
rca of the issue: Active-state accent color: NavItem at /app/frontend/src/components/layout/Sidebar.jsx line 78 declares className `bg-[var(--bp-primary,#d9b285)]`. The CSS variable --bp-primary is globally bound to the theme's teal #00c9b3 (visible also on 'Cultural Edition™' CTA button and ™ marks). Since the var IS defined, the #d9b285 fallback never activates. Spec demands gold accent. Mitigation: replace with `bg-[#d9b285]` literal or introduce a separate --bp-accent-gold token in the design system root and use it on accent strip + ™ marks for consistency.
